_about: Research for a seasonal yard-sale map layer in Out's Events tab (separate from the newsletter calendar, which excludes yard sales). Every source carries source_url and verified.

sources.name: Front Porch Forum calendar
sources.coverage: Chittenden County neighborhood forums; calendar pages show events from many nearby towns (Burlington, South Burlington, Colchester, Shelburne, Richmond, Winooski, St. Albans seen)
sources.machine_readable: Technically yes: calendar pages (/<forum-slug>/calendar, 3–7 MB HTML) and event pages (/calendar/events/<id>) load with plain curl + browser UA, and event pages show the street address under 'Event Info' plus start/end times. No feed or API.
sources.terms_of_use_note: FPF Terms of Use prohibit aggregating, copying or displaying Content and using 'data mining, robots, spiders, or other data gathering and extraction tools for any purpose' (exception only for search engines and non-commercial archives). The repo's data/sources.json already records a standing POLICY: FPF is never scraped.
sources.sample_count_note: 63 yard/garage/estate/moving/rummage/porch-sale events on the South Burlington Central calendar page (window roughly late Sept to Nov 2026); 20 on the Old North End calendar page. Examples: 'Last Yard Sale of the Year - East Main St - Oct. 24', 'Rummage Sale at Richmond Congregational Church'. Most are now past.
sources.seasonality: Heavy in September–October in today's sample; titles like 'Last Yard Sale of the Year' (Oct 24) suggest the season winds down late October.
sources.recommendation_note: Best real-world coverage by far, but ToS and Stephen's standing policy rule out scraping. Use it to invite sellers to submit to Out themselves, or ask FPF for permission/partnership.

sources.machine_readable: No: the RSS URL (?format=rss) returned 403 'blocked'; the HTML page has JSON-LD but the ItemList was empty, with listings rendered as text.

sources.sample_count_note: 4 listings on the page; Chittenden County ones were a moving sale (Sat Oct 31 & Sun Nov 1, Essex Junction) and a bazaar (Essex Jct). Town only, no street addresses on the list.

related_rule.rule: Winooski only allows temporary lawn signs in public rights-of-way if they are campaign signs (two weeks before to shortly after an election) or nonprofit signs approved by the city manager; one per entity per 50 feet.

sources.name: Reader submissions to Out (proposed)
sources.machine_readable: Yes, by design (own form → own database).
sources.terms_of_use_note: Our own terms; seller grants permission and confirms they live at / control the address.

simplest_viable_plan: Make reader submissions the only automated source: a short form (sale type, street address, town, date(s), start/end time, optional 3 photos of items, required photo of the sign or a confirmation link sent to the submitter's email/phone).

Geocode the address once on submission, snap the public pin to the block (or street centroid) until the sale day, and show the exact address only from 6 AM on the first sale day until the end time on the last day; then remove the pin and delete the address after the sale.
Hand-add public events (church rummage sales, town-wide or neighborhood sale days) as pinned events, since they are not private homes.
Link out (no copying) to EstateSales.NET for estate sales and tell FPF users they can post to Out too. Do not scrape FPF, Craigslist or the national yard-sale sites; all of them forbid it.
Seasonal window: show the layer mid-April through October (FPF sample shows activity through late October, e.g. 'Last Yard Sale of the Year' Oct 24); hide it November–March.
Moderate before publish (Stephen or a helper approves each pin) for the first season; auto-expire everything.
verification_options: Photo of the posted sign at the address (strong, easy for sellers)
Email or SMS confirmation link (cheap, stops drive-by spam)
privacy_notes: Home addresses are personal data: show the exact address only while the sale is live and drop it right after; never keep a history of past sale addresses.
Before the sale day show only the street/block or neighborhood, plus date and time.
No seller names or phone numbers on the map; contact goes through the form if needed at all.
Let sellers delete their pin at any time; remove pins reported as wrong.
stephen_must_decide: Whether to build a submission form and moderation queue at all (that is the real cost; there is no usable free feed).
Verification bar: sign photo required, or email/SMS confirmation only.
Exact-address timing: exact pin only during sale hours vs. from the morning of the first day.
Whether to ask Front Porch Forum for permission or a partnership (their calendar has the volume).
Season dates (proposed mid-April to end of October) and whether estate-sale companies may post (commercial).
Whether this conflicts with the newsletter's rule that keeps yard sales out of the calendar (the map would be a separate layer only).
